clue.text: Sleep over: in the morning getting a cover on top?

indicators.note: over signals turning the word for a short sleep the other way round

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
AM, ante meridiem, marks morning times
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping in and wondering whether they need a cover over them in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a playful description: a hat is literally a cover worn on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat, and a hat is a covering worn on the head.

clue.text: Outline for dossier

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a dossier is a file of papers on a person

explanation.surface: Someone asking for an outline to put in a dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a double definition, but for supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a side view or silhouette of something, its outline.

clue.text: Wants dress with inside taken out before wedding begins

indicators.note: begins puts the wedding piece at the start

parts.note: née introduces a woman's name before she married

indicators.note: the middle letters of dress are removed, leaving its outside

parts.note: the word dress itself is the fodder, stripped down to its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to have a dress altered before the wedding starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before wedding' is not a time but née, as in 'Jane Smith, née Jones'.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs and wants are synonymous as verbs: to require or lack something.

clue.text: Christmas card nearly missing kiss on one 18 across

indicators.note: the kiss is left out of what remains
nearly cuts off the final letter of the card phrase

parts.note: Christmas is often written Xmas
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A Christmas card lacking its usual kiss, with a cosmetic stuck on.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is COSMETIC, so the definition is a cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is make-up for the eyelashes, an example of a cosmetic.

clue.text: Field runs across river: it's outstanding

indicators.note: the field stretches across the runs, so the word for field is placed around their letter

parts.note: an area is a field or region
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring runs across a field by a river, with a remark that the play is outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is more often plural, but Collins and Chambers both list the singular for a sum still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrear is a debt or payment still unpaid, something left owing and so outstanding.

clue.text: Comes back on with performers

parts.note: re means on or concerning
turns are acts on a variety bill, so performers

explanation.surface: A comeback by a group of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to come back, the plain synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Hand over one tenner initially during uninitiated prostitution

indicators.note: the one and the tenner's letter come during, inside, the trade word
the first letter of the prostitution phrase is dropped

parts.note: prostitution is the sex trade
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the first letter of tenner is taken

parts.note: the word tenner supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tenner handed over to a novice prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over' reads as paying the money, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to hand over a suspect to another country's legal authorities.

clue.text: Some line Kate rehearsed in recess is filmed again

indicators.note: to recede is to go back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of line, all of Kate and the start of rehearsed

explanation.surface: An actor named Kate rehearsing a line during a break from filming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a break in rehearsals, but it signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene retaken is shot once more, a cinema term for filming something a second time.

clue.text: Let bachelor nurse beer, getting round

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: the beer goes round the bachelor's letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A bachelor allowed to nurse a pint while buying a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse beer' suggests sipping a pint slowly, but nurse and beer are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to allow or permit it, so let.

clue.text: Its union meets regularly with working group

indicators.note: working means these letters are being worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word with, the first and third

parts.note: the word with itself, whose first and third letters are taken

explanation.surface: A description of a women's organisation whose branch members gather at regular meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meets regularly' reads as one phrase about the group's habits, but regularly works only on 'with'. The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women, known for jam-making and local meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Women's Institute is a national organisation of local clubs, a group whose members meet together.

clue.text: Party: go to one to consume drugs

indicators.note: the word for go swallows the drugs, so their letters sit inside it

parts.note: to go somewhere is to fit there, as a jigsaw piece goes or fits in its place
E is slang for ecstasy, so Es are drugs
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: An invitation to head to a party and take drugs there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb of travel, but it means fit, as in where a piece goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, originally Spanish, so it is a party.

clue.text: Boozer stands and jeers

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, which is a bar
racks are stands for holding things

explanation.surface: A drinker in a pub gets up and heckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' reads as a drinker but means a pub, the British slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to shout down a speaker or player with derisive heckling, the same as jeering.

clue.text: Cover for work by old master

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker covering for an absent employee
late means former or dead, so old

explanation.surface: A painting by an Old Master and someone covering for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' reads as a great painter, but old supplies its letters separately and master alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is an original from which copies are made, which is what a template is: a pattern.

clue.text: Bent police, ultimately: head is out of prison first

indicators.note: first places the shortened prison at the front
the letters of is are removed from prison

parts.note: the word prison itself is used
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of police is taken

parts.note: the word police supplies its final letter
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A corrupt police officer whose boss is just out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as corrupt, British slang for a dishonest officer, but it means an inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural tendency or inclination, as is proneness.

clue.text: As one Grand National horse at the back is well-groomed

parts.note: so can mean as, in comparisons such as 'not so tall'
I is the Roman numeral one
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: the last letter, at the back of the word horse, is taken

parts.note: the word horse supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A horse running in the Grand National, the famous British steeplechase, trailing at the back but nicely turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known horse race, which makes Grand National read as a single name rather than two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soigné is a French borrowing for someone elegantly dressed and carefully presented, i.e. well-groomed.

clue.text: Digs introduction to Starsky and Hutch special

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so the opening letter of Starsky is taken

parts.note: the name Starsky supplies its first letter
a hutch is an animal pen, as is a coop

explanation.surface: The opening of a special episode of the police TV series Starsky and Hutch.
explanation.walkthrough: Starsky and Hutch reads as the American cop show, but Hutch means an animal cage.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoop is to dig out or excavate, as with a spoon or shovel.

clue.text: Draw together detailed picture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring together or close a gap
second meaning: a photo or shot taken from very near

explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks artistic alongside picture, but in the first sense it means pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Close up as a verb joins edges; a close-up is a photograph taken at short range showing detail.

clue.text: Flog small bottle, no adult present

indicators.note: no adult present means the adult's letter is taken away

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, nerve

explanation.surface: Selling a small bottle of alcohol when no grown-up is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as sell, but it means whip; bottle is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip someone, so it means flog in its sense of beat.

clue.text: Concerned with stars describing film that's superficial

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the stars word goes round the film

parts.note: cosmic means relating to the cosmos and its stars
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A judgement that a film about the stars is shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' means drawing a line around, as in geometry, rather than giving an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic change affects only the appearance and not the substance, so it is superficial.

clue.text: Rubs clue out essentially going with answer

indicators.note: going means departing, so the letter named leaves the word clue
essentially points to the essence or heart of the word out, its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of out

explanation.surface: A solver erases a clue from the page, dealing with it and its answer together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the instruction to remove, but it is the word whose centre, 'essentially', is the U that is 'going' from clue, leaving CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean something is often to scrub or wipe it, so cleans works as a synonym for rubs.

clue.text: One teases, initially showing chest

indicators.note: the first letter of showing is taken

parts.note: the word showing supplies its first letter
a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: A tease who starts by revealing their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing chest' suggests flirting, which fits teases but is mere surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoffer mocks and jeers at others, someone who teases or ridicules.

clue.text: Briefly at home, separate to get over husband

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the separating word goes over and covers the husband's letter

parts.note: to sort is to separate into groups

explanation.surface: A couple briefly at home, separating so one can get over the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is an idiom meaning to sum up concisely, the same as briefly.

clue.text: Well, look, hero is back in bed, getting end away

indicators.note: the reversed hero and the look are placed inside the shortened bed
the final letter of bed is removed

parts.note: the word bed itself is used before its end goes

indicators.note: is back applies to look and hero together, so both are read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
the word hero itself, read backwards with look

explanation.surface: A cheeky account of a hero back in bed and getting his end away, British slang for having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting his end away' is British slang for having sex; here it just drops the final letter of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A borehole is a narrow shaft drilled into the ground for water or oil, a kind of well.

clue.text: Relating to one in school that's unfriendly?

parts.note: of means concerning or relating to
fish swim in schools, so one in a school is a fish

explanation.surface: A query about whether a pupil at school is standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests pupils, but it is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish is an informal word for aloof or distant in manner, so unfriendly.

clue.text: Put up painting of leaf

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means reading from the bottom upward, so backwards

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hanging a painting of a leaf on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' reads as hanging a picture, but in a down entry it signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a single sheet of a book or manuscript, a leaf in the bookbinding sense.

clue.text: Hit green in place for birdie

indicators.note: the letters are struck and knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Golf advice: hit onto the green in the right place to score a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word looks like golf, and birdie seems to mean one under par; it is the ordinary word for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a bird of prey, so a birdie in the childish sense of a bird.

clue.text: Supplier of escort to follow prince

indicators.note: the escort word comes after the prince's letter

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: Someone supplying an escort to walk behind a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplier' reads as innocent, but a pusher is a drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pusher is a slang term for someone who sells or supplies illegal drugs.

clue.text: Shot down pilot

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try
down and out go together: a batsman out is down, done for

explanation.surface: An aircraft pilot shot down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an airman shot down; pilot is the test-run sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial run of a scheme or programme, a test before full adoption.
